svg.title: Eight frames. The rerun battled every team against all 50 meta files with the six Pokemon shuffled before each battle. An edit changes one thing on one Pokemon, in one of six kinds, and each kind is tried 3 times on a team. Replays of the unchanged team show battle noise, about 3.40 points. With noise removed, one edit moves win rate by 5.90 points for a whole Pokemon swap, 4.84 for a move, 4.35 for an item, 3.66 for an ability, 1.95 for stat alignment and 1.60 for Stat Points. No size cutoff is used. Four kinds have a 95% interval above zero from tournament-ready teams, and the two Stat kinds do not. As a share of the 9.04-point spread between teams, the whole Pokemon swap is 0.65, larger than one step on the Pest Control benchmark, which is 0.37 of the spread between its random starting points and 0.32 between its hill-climbed ones. Move, item and ability edits are undecided against that step. From search-found teams only the whole Pokemon swap and the move edit are above zero.

A replay shows how far a score moves by luck
alone. That move is battle noise.

For the whole Pokemon swap: 6.81 squared minus

7. Is the edit large? Its share of the spread between teams, against one step on a
The yardstick is a benchmark, not a number someone
picked. Each size is divided by how far teams'
scores spread, 9.04 points. One step on Pest
Control is 0.37 of the spread between its random
starting points, and 0.32 between its hill-climbed
A whole Pokemon swap is 0.65 of the spread, and
its interval clears the step. Move, item and
ability edits sit above the step, but their
intervals reach it, so they are undecided.
